world_status: a description exists but is not accessible

earlier_scan.source_named: Lecoq, Pierre. 1979. Le Dialecte de Sivand. Wiesbaden: Reichert.
earlier_scan.note: Full grammar of Sivandi exists (also Mann & Hadank 1926 sketch; Christensen 1939); none found online.

sources.citation: Mann, Oskar & Karl Hadank. 1926. Die Mundarten von Khunsâr, Mahallât, Natänz, Nâyin, Sämnân, Sîvänd und Sô-Kohrûd (Kurdisch-persische Forschungen, Abt. III, Bd. 1). Berlin/Leipzig: de Gruyter. Sivändi: pp. 223-231; intro '(f) Vom Sivändi' pp. XCVI-XCVII.
sources.access_detail: a copy the project holds (available on request)
sources.note: Nothing. The Sivandi part is one fable recorded by O. Mann (1907), a word-comparison table, a bare 'Lautbestand' (vowel/consonant inventory, p. 225), notes 'Zu den Lautverhältnissen' (kh^w > f, v/w/u alternation, p. 225-226), verb forms and a glossary; Hadank states 'Die Untersuchung des einzigen zur Verfügung stehenden Textes reicht nicht aus zur Klärung aller grammatischen Fragen' (p. 225). No word Betonung/Akzent/Ton/Druck occurs in pp. 223-231 (scanned a full-text search for stress/accent).

sources.citation: Wikipedia, 'Sivandi language' (en), 'زبان سیوندی' (fa), 'Sivandi' (fr); Glottolog 5.3 siva1239 page.
sources.note: None of them says anything about stress. fa.wikipedia gives a phoneme inventory only (25 consonants, 8 vowels, 3 diphthongs, unsourced) and cites Eilers 1988, Andreas/Christensen 1939, Lentz 1926, Windfuhr 1975 among others; en.wikipedia cites Windfuhr 1991 (EIr 'Central dialects') and Skjærvø 1990.

sources.citation: Khorram Sivandi, M. 2015. Grammar of the Sivandi. Shiraz: Sivand Publishing.
sources.tag: likely states stress; not yet obtained
sources.note: Most recent native-speaker grammar (Glottolog grammar sketch); likely source of the phoneme inventory on fa.wikipedia; may state stress.

sources.citation: Eilers, Wilhelm (ed.), bearb. mit Ulrich Schapka. 1988. Die Mundart von Sīvänd (Westiranische Mundarten aus der Sammlung Wilhelm Eilers, Bd. 3). Stuttgart: Steiner. XX+376 pp.

sources.note: Largest description of Sivandi (grammar sketch, texts, glossary from Eilers' 1950s-60s fieldwork); the companion Chunsar and Gäz volumes have explicit Betonung sections. Reviews: Skjærvø JAOS 110(4):787-788; Weber BSOAS 56(2):378-379.
